items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The line-up was Jimmy Archey, trombone... Red Allen and myself, trumpets.

ctx.x: As for socializing with the clientele was concerned, no band, white or coloured, was allowed to do that. And everyone, clients, musicians, bartenders and hostesses came in and went out the front door. We came and left by a back door at the Roseland.

Russel was now employing three trumpets and Higginbotham was not there. The line-up was Jimmy Archey, trombone, Henry 'Moon' Jones had replaced Charlie Holmes on alto sax, Greely Walton had replaced Teddy Hill on tenor-sax, Albert Nicholas, alto-sax and clarinet, Bill Johnson, guitar, Paul Barbarin, drums, Pops Foster, bass, Bill Dillard, Red Allen and myself, trumpets. And this time I had more solos and played some of the first parts also.

One night the orchestra of Noble Sissle who was working in a big white hotel was engaged at the Arcadia to play a battle of jazz between Russell and the other white orchestra whose name I don't remember. I had seen Sissle on stage when I was in Cincinnati and in my estimation he was pretty much a ham actor. So it was a night that we were looking forward to, and the Uncle Tom in him was really shown when his band came in dressed in red frocktail coats which made them look like a circus monkey band. There were some…

items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: alter from Tommie Benford saying that he could not join me for the tour because he had been playing in the orchestra of Jimmy Arche for a few years

ctx.x: I would doze until I felt the train slowing down and then jump to the window to see if we were coming into the place where I was supposed to change. The conductor don't come through to announce the next station as they do in the U.S.A., Switzerland and Germany. So I was jumping up all night until 4 a.m. when a conductor finally came through. He told me that I didn't have to change trains because this one went to Sete directly. The train arrived at my destination at 5'15 a.m. and I was certainly in a bad humour…

I played two dates in Sete, one in a place called Agde, another in Amelie les Bains and two in Perpignan and left there the 4th of September for Paris because I had to see a lawyer there who was in charge of getting me a divorce from my wife Madelyn. I returned to Chamonix the 5th and there was alter from Tommie Benford saying that he could not join me for the tour because he had been playing in the orchestra of Jimmy Arche for a few years and Jimmie would be coming to Europe at a later date so he decided to stay…

The 10th of September, I had to leave Chamonix for Geneva, Switzerland, where I was to take a train for Hannover, Germany to begin the 21 days tour of that country. The concert tour of France was to begin the 13th of October. Lily was to leave for Paris in a few days and would inquire about a drummer to replace Tommy Benford.
